sentences.text: Imagine a library that has grown so large that a single building can no longer hold all the books.

sourceRef.title: The Sharding Pattern: Scaling Data Stores Horizontally

sentences.text: Instead of building one impossibly large structure, you create multiple library branches—each holding books organized by a specific category or range.

sourceRef.title: The Sharding Pattern: Scaling Data Stores Horizontally

sentences.text: Patrons know which branch to visit based on what they're looking for.

sourceRef.title: The Sharding Pattern: Scaling Data Stores Horizontally

sentences.text: This is the essence of sharding: dividing data across multiple stores to overcome the limitations of a single server.

sourceRef.title: The Sharding Pattern: Scaling Data Stores Horizontally

sentences.text: Just as a library system with multiple branches:↵Distributes books across locations↵Allows parallel access by many patrons↵Reduces crowding at any single location↵Enables geographic proximity to users↵A sharded data store:↵Distributes data across multiple servers↵Allows parallel queries and writes↵Reduces contention on any single database↵Enables data locality for better performance↵

sourceRef.title: The Sharding Pattern: Scaling Data Stores Horizontally

sentences.text: A data store hosted on a single server faces inevitable constraints:

sourceRef.title: The Sharding Pattern: Scaling Data Stores Horizontally

sentences.text: ↵:::warning{title="Vertical Scaling Limitations"}↵**Temporary Solution**: Adding more CPU, memory, or disk to a single server↵**Physical Limits**: Eventually you can't add more resources↵**Cost Inefficiency**: High-end servers become exponentially expensive↵**Single Point of Failure**: One server failure affects all users↵:::

sourceRef.title: The Sharding Pattern: Scaling Data Stores Horizontally

sentences.text: Divide the data store into horizontal partitions called shards.

sourceRef.title: The Sharding Pattern: Scaling Data Stores Horizontally

sentences.text: Each shard:↵Has the same schema↵Contains a distinct subset of data↵Runs on a separate storage node↵Operates independently↵

sourceRef.title: The Sharding Pattern: Scaling Data Stores Horizontally

sentences.text: Use a mapping table to route requests to the appropriate shard:↵ ↵ ↵:::tip{title="Lookup Strategy Benefits"}↵**Flexibility**: Easy to rebalance by updating the map↵**Virtual Shards**: Map logical shards to fewer physical servers↵**Control**: Assign high-value tenants to dedicated shards↵:::

sourceRef.title: The Sharding Pattern: Scaling Data Stores Horizontally

sentences.text: Group related items together based on sequential shard keys:↵ ↵ ↵:::tip{title="Range Strategy Benefits"}↵**Range Queries**: Efficiently retrieve sequential data↵**Natural Ordering**: Data stored in logical order↵**Time-Based Archival**: Easy to archive old shards↵:::↵:::warning{title="Range Strategy Risks"}↵**Hotspots**: Recent data often accessed more frequently↵**Uneven Distribution**: Some ranges may grow larger than others↵:::

sourceRef.title: The Sharding Pattern: Scaling Data Stores Horizontally

sentences.text: Distribute data evenly using a hash function:↵ ↵ ↵:::tip{title="Hash Strategy Benefits"}↵**Even Distribution**: Prevents hotspots↵**No Lookup Table**: Direct computation of shard location↵**Scalable**: Works well with many shards↵:::↵:::warning{title="Hash Strategy Challenges"}↵**Range Queries**: Difficult to query ranges efficiently↵**Rebalancing**: Adding shards requires rehashing data↵:::

sourceRef.title: The Sharding Pattern: Scaling Data Stores Horizontally

sourceRef.title: The Sharding Pattern: Scaling Data Stores Horizontally

sentences.text: The shard key determines data distribution and query performance:↵ ↵:::anote{title="Shard Key Best Practices"}↵**Immutable**: Choose keys that never change↵**High Cardinality**: Many unique values for even distribution↵**Query Aligned**: Support your most common query patterns↵**Avoid Hotspots**: Prevent sequential keys if using hash strategy↵:::

sourceRef.title: The Sharding Pattern: Scaling Data Stores Horizontally

sentences.text: :::success{title="Use Sharding When"}↵**Massive Scale**: Data volume exceeds single server capacity↵**High Throughput**: Need to handle millions of concurrent operations↵**Geographic Distribution**: Users spread across multiple regions↵**Cost Optimization**: Multiple commodity servers cheaper than one high-end server↵:::↵:::warning{title="Avoid Sharding When"}↵**Small Scale**: Data fits comfortably on one server↵**Complex Joins**: Application relies heavily on cross-table joins↵**Limited Resources**: Team lacks expertise to manage distributed systems↵**Premature Optimization**: Vertical scaling still viable↵:::

sourceRef.title: The Sharding Pattern: Scaling Data Stores Horizontally

sentences.text: **Scalability**: Add more shards as data grows↵**Performance**: Parallel processing across shards↵**Cost Efficiency**: Use commodity hardware instead of expensive servers↵**Geographic Proximity**: Place data close to users↵**Fault Isolation**: Failure in one shard doesn't affect others

sourceRef.title: The Sharding Pattern: Scaling Data Stores Horizontally

sentences.text: **Complexity**: More moving parts to manage↵**Cross-Shard Queries**: Expensive fan-out operations↵**Rebalancing**: Difficult to redistribute data↵**Referential Integrity**: Hard to maintain across shards↵**Operational Overhead**: Monitoring, backup, and maintenance multiply
